column12: Judgement on timing. Book convention (calderasib and LY3537982 seeds): first full year two calendar years after the Phase 3 primary completion, so readout late 2029, filing 2030, launch late 2030, 2031 the first full year. The asset's earliest Phase 3 primary completion is RASolute 305 in pancreatic cancer (2028-12-30), which would give 2030 if that indication were modelled; NSCLC revenue cannot start before its own readout. Case for earlier: FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in December 2025 (RVMD FY2025 10-K 0001193125-26-071563; press coverage dates it January 2026) for previously treated KRAS G12D NSCLC, with a Phase 2 monotherapy expansion still following patients (10-Q Q2 2026). An accelerated second-line approval would come earlier, but in a different line and pool, and RVMD has stated no such filing. LOE: no molecule patent date is filed. Revolution's FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-071563, patents section) gives only a 2031 to 2045 range across its tri-complex RAS portfolio, with no date for zoldonrasib, so the engine's default applies: 12 years from this launch year, 2043. column12: Wholly owned: zoldonrasib comes from RVMD's own RAS(ON) discovery pipeline, and the filings name no licensor or co-development partner; the Summit (ivonescimab) and Tango collaborations are clinical combination studies with no stated economics on zoldonrasib. Daraxonrasib's only approval is in pancreatic cancer and its NSCLC Phase 3 (RASolve 301) is in previously treated disease, so a first-line G12D NSCLC label does not sit inside a daraxonrasib indication today and the royalty does not attach. Case against: if daraxonrasib later wins a first-line NSCLC label (RVMD is testing it with PD-(L)1/VEGF bispecifics), the royalty attaches at 4.55% of annual net sales up to $2.0bn, 2.50% from $2.0bn to $4.0bn and 1.00% from $4.0bn to $8.0bn after the two tranches drawn, rising to 7.80%, 4.55% and 2.40% if tranches 3 to 5 are drawn, with an upward adjustment in 2030 to 2041 on the first tier if sales fall short. RVMD has no cost rows in the book, so the netting (margin - royalty) / margin cannot be computed yet. Second reader's case against: the 10-Q defines the royalty base as worldwide net product sales of RMC-9805 Products once an RMC-9805 Product is approved in an indication inside an RMC-6236 one, and does not say the base is only that indication. Royalty Pharma's release ('zoldonrasib if approved in an overlapping daraxonrasib indication') supports the per-indication reading used here. If the agreement is product-wide, a first-line G12D PDAC approval from RASolute 305 (primary completion 2028-12-30), inside a first-line daraxonrasib PDAC label from RASolute 303 (2028-06), would bring the NSCLC sales under the royalty before 2031. The tiers are struck on combined daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib sales, so the marginal rate would most likely be 2.50%, 1.00% or nil. Tranche 3's trigger was met by the 2026-08-26 approval; no draw is filed yet

(1) KRAS G12D in 684 of 17,095 NSCLC specimens, 4.00% (Judd et al., 'Characterization of KRAS Mutation Subtypes in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer', Mol Cancer Ther 2021;20(12):2577-2584, doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-21-0201, PMID 34518295, Table 1; Caris, the paper the calderasib seed already cites for PD-L1). (3) 79% of US stage IV NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations start first-line therapy (2,904 of 3,661; Abernethy et al., PLoS One 2017, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0178420, the LY3537982 and ABBV-1480 seeds' share). 0.04001 x 0.51 x 0.79 = 0.016121, about 3,106 patients a year on 192,650. column12: No PD-L1 filter: the first-line Phase 1 cohort enrolled at every PD-L1 level (TPS <1% in 39%, 1-49% in 39%, 50% or more in 16%; RVMD Q2 2026 release, 8-K 0001193125-26-335039) and the pembrolizumab-pemetrexed-platinum backbone is labelled regardless of PD-L1, as in the LY3537982 seed. RASolve 308's eligibility (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07777822) requires previously untreated metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with a documented RAS G12D mutation and a known PD-L1 status, with no PD-L1 threshold, so no PD-L1 filter applies. Case for higher: Judd's G12C share (1,882 of 17,095, 11.0%) sits below the 13.8% GENIE figure the G12C seeds use, so this Caris cohort may understate allele shares against GENIE; and the trial's 'RAS G12D' includes NRAS and HRAS G12D, which Judd does not count. Case for lower: the 4.0% includes squamous tumours the trial excludes (KRAS is mutated in 4.4% of squamous against 37.2% of adenocarcinoma, so the effect is small), and the 51% is all lung cancer, where SCLC skews distant. Stage IV recurrences after early-stage disease are left out, which understates the pool.
